ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, authorised signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and domestic sanctions administered under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004, together with the FIC Guidance Notes (notably Guidance Note 6 on politically exposed persons). Politically exposed persons must be subjected to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval before any corporate relationship is established.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za) - online name reservation application (CoR 9.1)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be expressed in Latin (Roman) alphabetic characters and may be in any of South Africa's official languages rendered in the Latin script. No transliteration certificate is required for English or Afrikaans names. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing names, must not be merely descriptive of the business in a way that offends a section 11(2) ground, and must end with the prescribed suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or the abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd' for a private company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank (requires prior consent of the South African Reserve Bank)
Insurance / Assurance (requires prior consent of the Financial Sector Conduct Authority)
Auditing / Auditor (requires prior consent of the Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors)
Attorney / Advocates / Legal (requires prior consent of the Legal Practice Council)
Medical / Dental (requires prior consent of the Health Professions Council of South Africa)
University / Technikon (requires prior consent of the Department of Higher Education and Training)
Stock Exchange (requires prior consent of the Financial Sector Conduct Authority)
President / Government / National / Provincial / Municipal (requires prior ministerial or executive approval)
Royal / Chamber of Mines / Organisation associated with a prominent institution (requires prior consent of the relevant authority)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The reserved name is valid for 20 business days from the date of the CIPC approval notice. If incorporation cannot be completed within the window, the applicant may file a further name reservation application for the same name where it remains available, or request an extension in writing to CIPC before expiry. If the name is rejected, CIPC issues a written decision citing the statutory ground. The applicant may (i) immediately re-submit a revised name reservation application containing a materially different name; (ii) within 15 business days of the rejection notice, apply to the Companies Tribunal for a review of the decision in terms of sections 12 and 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; and (iii) if the Companies Tribunal affirms the rejection, petition the High Court for judicial review in terms of the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000 within 180 days of the Tribunal decision. An appeal stops any other person from being granted the same name during the review period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible - the registered office must be a physical address situated in South Africa at which process may be served during business hours (section 23 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008). A 'virtual office' package comprising a physical street address, mail receipt, and occasional boardroom use is accepted by CIPC and SARS. A P.O. Box address or a purely remote non-physical address is prohibited. For the steel structure prefabricated building EPC industry, a commercial virtual registered office is acceptable provided the company maintains operational substance, including a bank account, employees, contracts, and identifiable project or site premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate (estimated 20-30% probability in the first operating year). CIPC does not conduct routine unannounced inspections of standard private companies, but SARS taxpayer compliance risk profiling, FIC reporting obligations, and municipal business-licence verification may trigger a physical site inspection where the UBO structure discloses anomalies or the registered office lacks substance evidence.

Company incorporation and registration fee for a proprietary limited company with standard MOI
Beneficial ownership register filing (UBO declaration and supporting schedule)
Notarisation of passport copies, MOI execution pages, shareholder resolutions, and affidavits (3-5 documents)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address service (virtual commercial office, first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered office service provider (business centre) in South Africa

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage 1 legal due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening, and name clearance coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee (R35,000-R50,000 for pre-incorporation due diligence)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign-language incorporation documents (where applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page market rate (R200-R450 per certified page)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (ss. 1, 11, 13, 14, 19, 63-65) read with the Companies Regulations, 2011 (Forms CoR 9.4, 14.1, 14.3, 33.2)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Proprietary Limited Company; a nominal share capital (e.g. 100 Non-Par Value shares) suffices. No escrow account is statutorily mandated; funds are placed at the company's free disposal unless contractually restricted by bank or project finance covenants.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That each subscriber to the Memorandum of Incorporation takes up the allotted shares and executes the subscription schedule annexed; (2) That the registered office is established at [address], Johannesburg, Gauteng, South Africa, and the Company Secretary is authorised to file such address with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission; (3) That the following persons are appointed First Directors: [Name 1], [Name 2], to hold office until the next annual general meeting; (4) That auditors are appointed and directors execute all statutory forms; (5) That the chairperson certify true extracts for all regulatory authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on CIPC e-Services for the proposed name and at least two alternate names. File Form CoR 9.4, pay the prescribed fee, and obtain a Name Reservation Certificate valid for 6 months. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing company and must comply with section 11 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
required_dossiers: Certified ID or passport copies of each incorporator and director
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
Draft Memorandum of Incorporation for name compliance review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or contested, file a fresh reservation under an alternate name, or apply for reconsideration by CIPC under regulation 14 of the Companies Regulations, 2011 using Form CoR 9.5 within 20 business days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services Portal; physical filings accepted at CIPC National Office, Pretoria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CoR 14.1 and attach the signed Memorandum of Incorporation, incorporating the reserved name, registered office address, director details, authorised share capital, and any special provisions. Submit electronically with the prescribed incorporation fee. Upon acceptance, CIPC issues a Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3) and assigns a company registration number.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 14.1A) signed by all incorporators
Consent to Act as Director (Form CoR 1.1A) for each director
Certified ID/passport copies of all directors
Registered office address confirmation and consent of occupier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CIPC defect or query notices are cured by amending and resubmitting the CoR 14.1 electronically within 21 business days; if registration is refused, lodge an objection or apply for a fresh incorporation after rectifying the stated deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Company Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3) and the updated Company Extract (CoR 33.2) from CIPC e-Services. Verify all registered office, director, auditor, and share capital particulars. Retain certified copies for bank account opening, SARS tax registration, and sectoral licensing.
required_dossiers: Filing receipt confirming payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any error in the company extract is corrected by filing a Notice of Amendment (CoR 15.3) with CIPC and paying the applicable amendment fee; alternatively apply for rectification in terms of section 163 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Statutory Employer Registrations (SARS, UIF and COIDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour - Unemployment Insurance Fund and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for Income Tax on SARS eFiling using the Certificate of Incorporation and obtain an Income Tax Reference Number. Register as an employer for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), Skills Development Levy (SDL), and Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF). Register with the Compensation Commissioner within 7 days of employing any staff under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) and obtain a Letter of Good Standing from the Compensation Fund.
required_dossiers: Director ID copies and power of attorney to SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS raises verification or rejects registration, resubmit the application via a SARS branch appointment with certified supporting documents and an executed SARS Power of Attorney; if the Compensation Fund queries COIDA registration, provide the corrected payroll detail and resubmit within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral, Municipal and Industrial Licensing (CIDB, Trading Licence, Building Plan and Environmental Authorisation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB); local municipality licensing department (e.g. City of Johannesburg); Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company on the CIDB Register of Contractors to obtain a contractor grading designation (GB classes) enabling lawful tendering and execution of steel structure and building works. Apply for a municipal business trading licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991 for the physical fabrication yard, submit building plans for municipal approval under the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400), and screen the proposed site under the NEMA Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations to determine whether a Basic Assessment, Full EIA, or exemption applies.
required_dossiers: CIDB e-Registration form and company extract
Building plan drawings compliant with SANS 10400
Fire and public health clearances for the fabrication yard
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or CIDB queries or refuses the application, cure the technical or zoning deficiencies and re-lodge within the appeal period; appeals lie to the municipal Licensing Appeal Board or the CIDB Appeals Tribunal, with formal notice filed within 30 days of the adverse decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB), local municipal licensing authority under the Business Act 71 of 1991, and the Department of Employment and Labour (OHSA enforcement)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CIDB Contractor Grading Registration (GB classes) and Municipal Business Trading Licence for metal fabrication and steel erection

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and provincial competent authority under the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998 (NEMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration or Basic Assessment (Listing Notice 1 - GN R983) for fabrication workshops and smaller steel structures; Full EIA Report (Listing Notice 2 - GN R984) for large-scale industrial facilities or developments exceeding the prescribed thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the National Water Act 36 of 1998 (Section 21 water use licence for wastewater discharge), National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 (Atmospheric Emission Licence for scheduled processes, including VOC and particulate limits in terms of GN 893 of 2020), and the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 for scrap steel and hazardous waste handling; wastewater discharge limits per the General Authorisation (GN 665) and gaseous emission limits per SANS 69 and NEM:AQA standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal fire department in terms of SANS 10400 Part B (fire protection) and NFPA codes; structural load inspection certificates per SANS 10162 (steel structural design) and SANS 10400; occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including baseline risk assessment, fall protection plan, first-aid kit, incident reporting, and construction regulation compliance (Regs 8-10).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — national tax and customs administration; primary digital portals are SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za) and the SARS Customs Declarations platform for SAD 500 lodgements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned South African (Pty) Ltd is incorporated under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 via the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC). Upon incorporation, CIPC transmits company data to SARS and an Income Tax Reference Number is issued automatically. The company must then (1) verify its SARS tax profile by uploading certified incorporation documents (Memorandum of Incorporation, COR14.1A, CIPC registration certificate) through eFiling or a SARS branch; (2) appoint a public officer resident in South Africa as required by s.246 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011; (3) register for Value-Added Tax using the VAT101 form via eFiling once taxable supplies exceed R1,000,000 in any 12-month period, or voluntarily from R50,000 (s.23 VAT Act 89 of 1991), with a separate VAT registration number issued upon approval; (4) register as an employer for PAYE/SDL/UIF using the EMP101e form where employees are appointed; and (5) obtain a SARS Customs Client Registration Number for export declarations. Non-resident directors and shareholders must disclose their foreign tax identification numbers or provide a certificate of non-resident tax status where a foreign TIN is unavailable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; classification follows legal form, so a (Pty) Ltd is a resident company taxed at entity level at the 27% corporate income tax rate applicable to years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023. Available statutory mechanisms include: (a) the s.12E small business corporation election where all shareholders are natural persons; (b) s.24J debt instrument accrual elections; (c) s.11D research and development allowance election requiring SARS pre-approval; (d) s.23F/23G group assessment elections for controlled group companies with common shareholding of at least 75%; and (e) anti-hybrid recharacterization mechanics under s.8E, s.8F, s.8FA, s.23K and s.23L that neutralize hybrid debt, hybrid equity and hybrid finance mismatches, including any elective treatment attached to those instruments, without conferring a general entity classification election on foreign investors.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration where taxable supplies exceed or can reasonably be expected to exceed R1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period (s.23(1)); voluntary registration permitted where taxable supplies exceed R50,000 in a 12-month period (s.23(2)); foreign suppliers of electronic services to South African residents are subject to a separate non-resident electronic services VAT registration regime effective 1 April 2019 without a local turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa presently does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls (CTC) or digital stamping for VAT invoices. A valid tax invoice must satisfy the content requirements of s.20 of the VAT Act and be issued within 21 days of the time of supply. SARS accepts electronic tax invoices and requires eFiling submission of VAT201 returns. The SARS eInvoicing pilot and a broader digitalization roadmap aligned with PEPPOL-style standardized e-invoice exchange are voluntary under the prevailing compliance regime; however, all customs export declarations (SAD 500) must be lodged electronically through the SARS Customs system, with API integration available to registered customs clients.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of steel structure goods under s.11(1)(a) of the VAT Act applies where: (i) goods are supplied under an agreement of sale to a non-resident recipient; (ii) the goods are exported from the Republic within 90 days of the date of supply, or within an extended period allowed by SARS ruling; and (iii) the vendor retains the documentary proof of export required by s.11(3). Offshore engineering and design services qualify for 0% VAT under s.11(2)(l) where physically rendered outside South Africa, or under s.11(2)(k) where supplied to a non-resident, provided the services are not excluded — in particular, services connected to immovable property situated in South Africa remain standard-rated, and prefabricated steel building kits physically exported as goods are best covered under s.11(1)(a) rather than the services provisions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500) lodged electronically via SARS Customs and endorsed as cleared for export
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export movement of the prefabricated steel units from a South African port to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice, signed sales order and EPC contract evidencing the supply to the non-resident
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds into a South African foreign exchange account
Packing list, certificate of origin and marine cargo insurance certificate (where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audit strategies target zero-rated export claims intensively. Where documentary proof is defective or the goods are not physically exported within the prescribed period, the supply is standard-rated at 15% and the VAT is assessed as a deemed supply under s.8(6) of the VAT Act, with interest from the date the tax should have been declared. Understatement penalties under s.222-223 of the Tax Administration Act range from 10% to 150% of the shortfall depending on conduct, and prescribed-rate interest (presently the repurchase rate plus 7 per cent) is charged under s.187 TAA. Administrative non-compliance penalties of up to R10,000 per month per return may be imposed under s.255 TAA. Fraudulent zero-rating arrangements — including phantom exports, over-invoicing, forged SAD 500 declarations or false bills of lading — attract additional tax of up to 200% of the tax evaded under s.59(1) of the VAT Act, criminal prosecution with possible imprisonment, and parallel exchange-control sanctions under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 where export proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), administering the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, as amended. FinSurv delegates day-to-day enforcement to Authorized Dealers (commercial banks) and Authorized Brokers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a bifurcated regime. Current account transactions (trade in goods and services, interest, royalties, and operational remittances) are freely convertible without prior SARB approval, provided an Authorized Dealer receives a completed Form TD001/TD002 and the supporting contract; the proceeds are then settled at the market ZAR exchange rate. Capital account transactions are highly regulated: inward foreign direct investment (share capital) is permissible under general permission, but must be reported via the SARB Foreign Investment (Form CFI) framework through the receiving Authorized Dealer; outward investment, financial assistance, and loans by residents to non-residents require FinSurv approval. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is lawful and uncapped subject to (i) audited distributable reserves, (ii) completed SARB Form DTF 212 (beneficial owner declaration for dividends), (iii) valid SARS Tax Compliance Status, and (iv) dividend withholding tax at 20% for dividends declared on or after 1 January 2025 (reduced to 5%–15% under an applicable Double Taxation Agreement). Structural hurdles include the Immovable Property (Restrictions) Act 12 of 2004 for any land-linked real estate investment and mandatory beneficial ownership disclosure under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under exchange control Regulation 7 read with FinSurv guidelines, full export proceeds must be repatriated to South Africa through an Authorized Dealer within 180 days from the date of shipment. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into ZAR: an exporter may retain 100% of the repatriated foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) at an Authorized Dealer or convert it at the prevailing market rate. Each export must be supported by a customs Bill of Entry (EX/ SAD 500 series) declaring the proceeds-repatriation obligation, and all commercial shipping documents must contain the standard exchange control clause to that effect. Failure to repatriate within the statutory window triggers: (i) breach notices from the Authorized Dealer and SARB, (ii) penalty interest on the unremitted amount, (iii) suspension or deregistration of the importer/exporter code with SARS, and (iv) potential criminal prosecution under the Currency and Exchanges Act. The exporter must also maintain a 5-year trade register evidencing shipment and payment records for SARB/SARS inspection.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
FirstRand Bank Limited (First National Bank - FNB Commercial)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility. An offshore digital EMI (e.g., FCA- or EU-licensed) holds no statutory standing to conduct South African banking business under the Banks Act 94 of 1990, and has no direct access to the SARB-operated South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) clearing system. Such an EMI may operate only through a white-label/correspondent arrangement with a SARB Authorized Dealer, or by obtaining a restricted banking licence from SARB - a materially costly and time-intensive process. Additional constraints include FICA section 21 operator obligations, FATCA and CRS reporting, and FinSurv policy that all ZAR cross-border flows must pass through an Authorized Dealer. Accordingly, for this steel-structure EPC treasury the recommended architecture is a primary domestic corporate account with SWIFT MT103/MT700 rails, not an offshore EMI. Feasibility rating: Low-Medium.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001) imposes a risk-based customer due diligence standard; it does not strictly mandate physical appearance if an equivalent electronic verification process is adopted. In practice, Tier-1 South African banks require at least one director or a notarized-power-of-attorney holder to complete a live video compliance interview, and most banks require an in-branch meeting for the principal signatory when the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident. Fully remote onboarding is nevertheless attainable where: (1) all beneficial owners provide notarised passport copies; (2) the CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register filing is produced; (3) a foreign bank reference confirming a 6-month relationship is supplied; (4) the company presents a current SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN; and (5) a video call is held with the bank's FICA officer. Banks may decline remote opening where the UBO resides in a FATF grey-listed jurisdiction. Typical onboarding completion time is 5 to 15 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner domiciled in a FATF grey-listed or high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passport and proof of residence; signed source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declaration; 6-month bank statements from the home jurisdiction; tax residence certificate / DTA article; reputable negative-news and sanctions screening report; corporate organigram evidencing the full ownership chain to the natural person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Steel prefab EPC contract with a state-owned or public-procurement end-buyer, raising corruption and trade-based money-laundering risk flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed EPC contract with scope and delivery schedule; SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN; B-BBEE certificate or exemption certificate; tender or competitive-procurement documents; proof of diligence and site approvals; copies of all public tender award notices; insurance and performance-bond documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inward capital injection (share premium exceeding ZAR 50 million) flagged as potential disguised loan or unexplained wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed SARB Form CFI notification filed via the Authorized Dealer; share subscription agreement; board resolution of the subscribing entity; independent valuation of the issued shares; source-of-funds evidence from the subscriber; audited financial statements; declaration confirming no encumbrance or off-balance-sheet financing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export proceeds sourced from multiple African transit hubs, triggering scrutiny of round-tripping or proceeds substitution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade file for every shipment: bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, pre-shipment inspection certificates (e.g., SGS, Intertek), customs EX1/SAD 500 acknowledgements, proof of duty payment at destination, rail/port transfer records, and the reconciling export register linking each invoice to the SARB-mandated repatriation deadline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient source-of-wealth transparency for an opaque (Pty) Ltd shareholding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC extract with Memorandum of Incorporation; Beneficial Ownership Register in prescribed form; audited group and local entity financial statements; audit opinion letter; home-country bank reference; explanatory affidavit setting out the group structure, commercial rationale, and revenue path; all documentation to be certified by a notary and, where required, apostilled.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for a non-resident parent injecting equity into the (Pty) Ltd: (1) instruct the remitting bank to dispatch a SWIFT MT103 with the equity-investment purpose code and clear reference to the Share Subscription Agreement; (2) the receiving Authorized Dealer credits the company's ZAR account or Foreign Currency Account only after obtaining the completed SARB Form CFI (foreign investment inflow), board resolution of the issuer, updated CIPC share register, and, for in-kind contributions, an independent valuation; (3) the Authorized Dealer performs OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening and FATCA/CRS self-certification before crediting; (4) the CFI report is submitted by the Authorized Dealer to FinSurv within 30 days of credit; (5) funds may remain in USD/EUR/GBP within the FCA or be converted to ZAR at the prevailing dealing rate; (6) any subsequent shareholder loan or financial-assistance inflow not structured as equity requires prior FinSurv approval under Regulation 3; (7) escrow-release instructions must be accompanied by the underlying EPC purchase orders to support the commercial purpose of the injected capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails permitted for trade settlement: (i) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for direct import payments to steel suppliers and subcontractors, supported by Form TD001/TD002, commercial invoice, bill of lading or AWB, customs entry, and inspection certificates; (ii) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit issued by the Authorized Dealer in SWIFT MT700/MT710 format, subject to UCP 600 documentary checking, covering raw steel and prefabricated components; (iii) Standby LCs and performance guarantees via SWIFT MT760 for EPC milestone obligations; (iv) ZAR-denominated payments to domestic subcontractors settled through the SARB SAMOS RTGS system; (v) all outflows must correspond to a genuine economic transaction, be submitted to the bank within 30 days of drawdown for exchange-control reporting, and avoid sanctioned persons in the steel supply chain. Where advance payment exceeds the normal trade cycle, the bank requires the underlying contract and may require a refund guarantee.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forward Exchange Contracts (FEC): bilateral ZAR-USD / ZAR-EUR / ZAR-GBP forwards booked with an Authorized Dealer against confirmed import or export invoices; standard tenor up to 12 months without special FinSurv approval; longer tenors require documented underlying exposure and SARB notice.

Cross-Currency Swaps and Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (USD-ZAR, EUR-ZAR): permitted for treasury balance-sheet hedging with a demonstrated underlying loan or trade liability, executed through an Authorized Dealer with SARB notification and full documentation of the economic purpose.

European-Style Vanilla Currency Options (call/put on ZAR): purchasable through an Authorized Dealer to hedge confirmed EPC bid or supply exposures; resident entities may not write options without prior FinSurv approval.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in ZAR: available to non-resident counterparties (parent hedging subsidiary exposure) in the offshore market; onshore resident corporates may access NDFs only in exceptional cases approved by the Authorized Dealer/SARB where no deliverable-market alternative exists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of ZAR 100 per Annual Return; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative deregistration (strike-off) of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) – Beneficial Ownership Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the CIPC Annual Return; updated within 7 business days after any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil and criminal penalties; each director may be liable up to ZAR 500,000 or imprisonment up to 10 years for knowingly false BO disclosures; CIPC may deregister the company for repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited or Independently Reviewed Annual Financial Statements (AFS) Compliance Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and CIPC (declared within annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be prepared within 6 months after the financial year-end; compliance status is declared in the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be held personally liable; failure to prepare AFS or comply with audit/review requirements is an offence attracting a fine up to ZAR 1 million or imprisonment up to 10 years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A compulsory independent audit applies where the company's Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more in the relevant financial year. If the PIS is between 100 and 349, an independent review is required. If the PIS is below 100, no audit or review is mandatory unless required by the company's MOI or shareholder agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS Standards (full) or IFRS for SMEs, as adopted in South Africa, using the Companies Act 2008 financial reporting standards and CIPC electronic filing taxonomy.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and file an annual confirmation with CIPC together with the annual return. The register must contain each beneficial owner's full name, identity/passport number, nationality, date and nature of acquisition or cessation of beneficial interest, and percentage of ownership. Any transfer or change of shareholding resulting in a beneficial ownership change must be lodged with CIPC within 7 business days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book
